thread_messages:
Jaime: Heads-up — ZenHealth SIG just pushed a BCP/DR section. They want RTO/RPO, backup cadence, failover architecture, SLA, and evidence of a recent DR test. Need a concise set of answers + artifacts for the POC. EOD tomorrow. @Priya @Liam

Priya: Got it. Which deployment are they currently testing? Hosted API or planning Dedicated?

Jaime: POC is Hosted API, production target is Dedicated. They specifically asked if Hosted has an SLA and what our RTO/RPO looks like.

Priya: Short answers to send back now: Hosted: multi-az active service with automated regional failover; no contractual SLA on the free/public Hosted tier — we recommend Dedicated for SLA-backed uptime. Typical operational RTO for hosted incidents (platform failover) is ~30–60 mins depending on failure class; RPO for request processing is effectively 0 for stateless requests, but client-side sessions/KV caches are best-effort.

Priya: Dedicated: SLA available (example: 99.95% for network+service availability on Dedicated contracts), cross-region replication optional, targeted RTO 15–60 mins depending on failover policy, RPO configurable down to <5 minutes with streaming replication.

Liam: Adding security posture bits: backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.2+). Persistent state (customer artifacts, billing metadata) is snapshotted every 6 hours by default; Dedicated customers can configure snapshot frequency and retention. We keep 30 days of rolling snapshots by default; longer retention via archive.

Liam: We run quarterly DR playbooks and annual full DR exercises for Dedicated customers. We can provide a redacted DR test report (summary + timings) and an excerpt of the runbook. Last redacted test we can share: 2026-01-15 — failover completed in ~12 minutes; validated traffic and KV cache repopulation; no data loss for persisted objects (RPO ~0).

Jaime: Perfect. Can you paste a short runbook excerpt I can include in the response? Prefer 5–8 steps.

Priya: Sure — excerpt below (sanitized):

```
1) Trigger failover: set failover flag in control plane (api: POST /internal/failover)
2) Promote standby region: run promote script on region-b (./promote_region.sh region-b)
3) DNS cutover: update CNAME TTL=60 -> point to region-b gateway
4) Verify health: smoke-test /health and /v1/generate on 3 nodes, expect 200s
5) Rehydrate caches: kick cache-repop job (kubectl -n runtime job cache-repop)
6) Validate persistent storage: run object-store consistency check (checksum diff)
7) Postmortem steps: collect logs, tag incident, notify customers via status page
```

Priya: Note — exact commands and script names are customer/private for Dedicated; this is a sanitized sequence appropriate for an external summary.

Aria: I'll prepare the artifacts: (1) sanitized runbook excerpt, (2) redacted DR test summary PDF, (3) backup/retention policy, (4) pointer to SOC2 Type II on the customer portal. Legal needs to sign off on redactions — I'll loop them in.

Liam: Also include our monitoring/alerting coverage: paged on P0 incidents, automated failovers for node/network level, and runbook-owned SLOs. We can state default monitoring retention (metrics 90d, traces 30d) and alerting thresholds if they ask.

Jaime: Good. Two follow-ups from the buyer: (A) They want evidence we actually ran the test — logs or ticket ID. (B) They asked about RPO guarantees for KV/session caches during failover.

Priya: For (A) we can provide a redacted incident ticket ID and the DR test summary (timestamped). Example: DR-20260115-01 (we'll redact internal agent names). For (B) session/KV caches are in-memory and best-effort; we recommend client-side checkpointing for session-critical workloads or Dedicated config with persistent KV (enabled with replication) that gives RPO <5m.

Liam: Quick compliance note to include: share only sanitized artifacts through the secure customer portal (not open Slack). I'll prepare a short paragraph about what to share and what to redact (no oncall notes, no internal IPs).

Jaime: Can we have the sanitized artifacts and the short answer draft by EOD tomorrow? The buyer flagged a compliance review blocker if we don't.

Aria: Yes — I'll coordinate with Legal and Security and upload to the secure portal. Expect a confirmation message in this thread when done.

OncallBot: Artifact DR-20260115-01-summary.pdf uploaded to secure portal (link expires in 7 days).

Jaime: Thanks everyone — I'll send the draft to the buyer once Aria confirms.

Priya: If they want an in-person runbook walk-through or a live failover demo for the POC, we can schedule a short session with SREs. That often clears blockers quickly.

Jaime: Noted. I'll ask them if they want a live demo. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
